hero.lead: A nation of 71.6 million at the heart of mainland Southeast Asia, where the World Bank backs low-carbon cities and carbon markets, and fewer than three in ten have safely managed sanitation.

capital.heading: Low-carbon cities and the markets to fund them.

register.name: Fifteen-year sustainability-linked bond with a nature target
register.detail: Public Debt Management Office · issued 17 September 2026 · 15 years · subscriptions 2.8 times the planned THB 15bn · about $750M · ADB technical assistance
register.note: The first sovereign sustainability-linked bond in Asia and the Pacific with a nature-related indicator
register.text: A fifteen-year bond of the Government of Thailand tied to two national targets: net greenhouse gas emissions of 152 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent by 2035, and at least 30% of land and inland water in protected areas and other conserved areas by 2030. It is tied to targets, not to named projects, so it is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Fifteen-year sustainability-linked bond (SLB406A)
register.detail: Public Debt Management Office · first issued 25 November 2024 · matures 17 June 2040 · coupon 2.70% · 14 issues to May 2026 · coupon moves 2.5 bp for each target
register.note: Thailand’s first sustainability-linked bond; THB 128.0bn was outstanding at the end of September 2025
register.text: The Kingdom of Thailand’s first sustainability-linked bond, enlarged over fourteen issues. Its coupon steps up or down by 2.5 basis points against two 2030 targets: greenhouse gas emissions of no more than 388,500 kilotonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, and 440,000 zero-emission cars and pick-ups registered in the year (122,796 in 2025). It is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Three-year sustainability bond, EXIM Thailand
register.detail: Export-Import Bank of Thailand · issued 20 June 2025 · due 2028 · coupon 1.78% · subscriptions over 2.4 times the issue size
register.note: The first tranche of a THB 6bn issue; the second is a five-year plain bond of THB 3bn at 1.90%
register.text: A sustainability bond of the state-owned Export-Import Bank of Thailand, whose proceeds go to green businesses and to social development, including access to finance for small and medium enterprises. It bears on the livelihood standard.

register.name: Low Carbon Cities and Carbon Market Development Project
register.detail: World Bank · approved 10 July 2026 · announced 13 July 2026 · project P514511 · Bangkok Metropolitan Administration the first participant
register.note: Up to 180 MW of renewable capacity and about 448 GWh of electricity saved a year; a further $2.4M supports carbon pricing policy
register.text: A World Bank-supported project for rooftop solar and energy-efficiency upgrades across public buildings, among them schools, healthcare facilities and district offices, and industrial estates, with Krungthai Bank bringing eligible carbon credits together for sale. It carries the energy standard and lowers the power bills of the schools and clinics that serve the education and health standards.

register.name: Resilient Transport Connectivity and Irrawaddy Dolphin Conservation Project
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · approved 22 December 2025 · project P509460 · Short Maturity Loan $38.98M, 7 years · IBRD Flexible Loan $101.78M, 11 years · PROBLUE grant $4M
register.note: The first World Bank lending operation in Thailand in 15 years; bridges across Songkhla Lake (7 km) and to Lanta (2 km)
register.text: A World Bank loan to build two bridges, across Songkhla Lake and from the Lanta islands to mainland Krabi, and to protect the Irrawaddy dolphin, with alternative livelihoods and less risk of entanglement in fishing gear. It is chiefly transport; its work on livelihoods bears on the livelihood standard for some of the 350,000 people it targets.

register.name: Climate-smart Health Services System Enhancement Project
register.detail: ADB · approved 15 June 2026 · loan 4785-THA · marked 15 October 2026 · total cost $302.21M, with $90.30M from the Government · Ministry of Public Health
register.note: ADB’s first loan to the Thai government in the health sector; specialist care for about 14 million people outside Bangkok
register.text: An ADB loan to upgrade and expand care at five public hospitals, in Chiang Mai, Nakhon Sawan, Kanchanaburi, Chanthaburi and Nakhon Ratchasima, with cancer, cardiac, surgical and trauma services and designs that resist floods and extreme weather. It carries the health standard and aims to cut referrals to Bangkok.

register.name: Notes and loans for women microentrepreneurs, Ngern Tid Lor
register.detail: IFC · approved 25 June 2026 · signed 3 August 2026 · invested 7 August 2026 · first tranche up to $25M in Tidlor’s debut yen notes · project 49981
register.note: At least 75% of the proceeds earmarked to women microentrepreneurs; IFC states the amounts are indicative
register.text: An IFC package of debt securities and loans to Ngern Tid Lor, a Thai lender to micro entrepreneurs and the self-employed, for on-lending to micro, small and medium enterprises. It carries the livelihood standard, with at least three quarters of the proceeds for women microentrepreneurs.

register.name: Solar and battery storage, Gulf Renewable Energy
register.detail: ADB · signed 6 February 2026 · ADB $75M · LEAP 2 $75M · DBS B loan $50M · parallel loans of $150M from DEG, DFIC and Export Finance Australia
register.note: 194 MW of solar (arithmetic: 126 MW with 151 MWh of storage, and 68 MW); about 191,550 tonnes of carbon dioxide avoided a year
register.text: A loan arranged by ADB for Gulf Renewable Energy, a subsidiary of Gulf Development, for two solar-plus-battery projects of 126 megawatts and a 68-megawatt solar plant. It bears on the energy standard, adding clean power to a grid that already reaches every home.

register.name: Loan for women-owned small businesses, Muangthai Capital
register.detail: ADB · signed 11 December 2025 · ADB $75M · $125M from six B lenders · ADB and SMBC lead arrangers
register.note: To expand financial inclusion to an estimated 200,000 women-owned micro, small and medium enterprises
register.text: An ADB loan to Muangthai Capital, a Thai lender, for women-owned micro, small and medium enterprises in rural Thailand. It carries the livelihood standard; women own or lead more than half of the nation’s small businesses.

register.name: Blue bond, East Water
register.detail: IFC among the investors · subscribed 18 August 2025 · IFC amount not disclosed
register.note: For the 553 km water transmission network of the Eastern Economic Corridor
register.text: A blue bond of East Water, which runs a 553-kilometre water transmission network in Thailand’s Eastern Economic Corridor, with IFC among its investors. Its proceeds free up cash flow to maintain the network; it bears on the water standard in a corridor expected to house 350,000 people by 2032.

register.name: Gender-inclusive social bond, Muangthai Capital
register.detail: IFC · announced 26 August 2024 · first tranche of up to $150M of senior debt approved 10 June 2024 · project 49396
register.note: Muangthai Capital is the first non-bank financial institution in Thailand to issue such a bond
register.text: An IFC investment in a social bond of Muangthai Capital whose proceeds are dedicated to loans for women-owned or women-led micro entrepreneurs. It carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: Loan for women-led and farm businesses, Ngern Tid Lor
register.detail: ADB · signed 13 June 2024 · in Thai baht · with technical assistance for a social finance framework
register.note: 75% of the financing for women-owned businesses, the rest for small enterprises in agribusiness
register.text: An ADB loan to Ngern Tid Lor for on-lending to underserved rural micro, small and medium enterprises, particularly those owned and led by women, and to firms in the farm value chain. It carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: Equity in the share offering of Thai Credit Bank
register.detail: IFC · approved 16 January 2024 · signed 18 January 2024 · invested 7 February 2024 · cornerstone investor · project 49009
register.note: The press release gives up to $23.8M (THB 844M); the disclosure page lists up to $30M equivalent
register.text: An IFC equity investment, as cornerstone, in the initial public offering of Thai Credit Bank, a lender to micro and small businesses, among them women-owned and women-led firms. It carries the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Rice, rubber and fruit across more than two fifths of the land.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2020
items.text: Beaches, temples and cities that draw visitors from every continent.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 14.4% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: A fifth of the power renewable, with sun and biomass to add.

items.name: Steps
items.text: A Bangkok social enterprise, certified as a B Corp, that gives the neurodivergent community training in employability and life skills and runs inclusive businesses such as coffee shops.

items.name: Local Alike
items.text: A pioneer of community-based tourism in Thailand that designs trips around villages’ own development plans, so that a significant portion of the profits is reinvested in the community.

items.name: DoiTung
items.text: The social enterprise of the Mae Fah Luang Foundation, selling coffee, macadamia, handicrafts and visits, which creates more than 1,500 formal jobs a year and income for over 2,500 households.

items.name: Jasberry
items.text: A social enterprise that works with over 2,500 small-scale farming households in northern Thailand to grow and sell Jasberry, an organic purple rice, to end farmer poverty.

items.name: Vulcan Coalition
items.text: A Thai company that trains and employs people with disabilities to build artificial intelligence services; more than 600 work with it, earning on average more than 9,000 baht a month.
